title: The critical strip
mathematical_role: Orient the reader to the critical strip, critical line, trivial/nontrivial zero distinction, pole at one, and functional-equation symmetry.
learning_objective: Read the complex-plane geometry of the Riemann hypothesis without confusing generic decorative points with verified zero data.
literal_semantics: The predecessor intends the central vertical line to stand for the critical line inside a vertical strip.
nonliteral_semantics: The generic dots are not source-bound nontrivial-zero coordinates.
The plate does not encode the pole at s=1.
The plate does not encode the negative-even trivial zeros.
The horizontal and vertical positions are not a calibrated complex-plane plot.

notes: A successor may use exact axes and source-bound zero data, but any finite zero set must remain visibly finite and provenance-bound.

reproducibility_notes: The predecessor is a hand-authored schematic rather than a plot generated from analytic or zero-location data.

accessibility.alt_text: Trivial zeros, the pole, symmetry, and nontrivial zeros are arranged around the critical line.
accessibility.long_description: The predecessor visually contains a strip, a central line, and generic dots, but does not actually display several structures named by its alternative text. The replacement must label Re(s), Im(s), Re(s)=0, Re(s)=1, Re(s)=1/2, the pole at one, trivial zeros, functional symmetry, and the provenance of any plotted nontrivial zeros.

claim_boundary.strongest_visual_claim: Pedagogical orientation to the analytic geography in which the Riemann hypothesis is stated.

supersession_reason: The predecessor's visible semantics do not match the structures promised by its title and description.
